text:
Nina Park: Quick ask for the feb webinar + benchmark blog launch. Need a creative manifest + first-pass assets by next Tue. Items: hero (desktop/tablet/mobile), benchmark visual pack (SVG + PNG exports), email header (600x200), two paid-ad crops (300x250, 160x600), slide deck master, and a one-page sales summary. Also need img alt text CSV and a short social copy matrix. Can design confirm?

Owen Lee: Copy that. Source data for the benchmarks is the latest run in /drive/benchmarks/mar2026 (csv + fig). Do we want raw charts or simplified illustrations?

Nina Park: Simplified charts for public blog (no raw axes), but include an appendix SVG with labelled axes for the one-pager. Key calls: lower median latency, predictable 99th pct, and cost/unit savings. Keep messaging tight for social.

Priya Malhotra: For localization: EN + FR required, ES optional. I'll queue translations after we lock the copy. Note: FR can expand ~12-18% so allow flexible text bounds in layouts.

Kai Torres: Got it. A few questions: 1) brand fonts (use system Inter variable or locked set?), 2) sponsor logos — cloudconf ok? monochrome? 3) CTA treatments?

Nina Park: Use locked set only (Inter + Redwood Display). CloudConf only, monochrome on dark band. Two CTA variants: "Register" (primary) and "Download benchmark" (secondary). We'll test on paid ad creative.

design-bot: Figma file created: "Mar Webinar - Benchmark Creative" https://www.figma.com/file/efgh5678/mar-webinar-assets - pages: comps, assets, exports. Export presets: web@1x/@2x, print-PDF 300dpi.

Owen Lee: For the benchmark visual pack, we want these visuals: 1) latency vs cost bar stack, 2) throughput heatmap with legend, 3) KV cache savings callout (percent), 4) rollout strategy diagram (canary -> a/b -> global). Keep colors within brand token set and ensure colorblind-safe palette for heatmap.

Priya Malhotra: I'll prepare the social copy matrix (short, mid, long) + French translations. Also will provide suggested hashtags and UTM templates.

Kai Torres: For the SDR one-pager, what fields do you want? I propose: headline (1 line), elevator (1 sentence), 3 bullets (differentiators), qualifying questions, routing rules, and suggested email subject lines.

Nina Park: Exactly. Add a small HubSpot routing snippet we can paste into workflows. Use this: 

```
WHEN Contact interacts with "webinar-2026-03-25" OR downloads "benchmark-1pager-2026"
THEN assign to queue: "SDR-Inbound-Webinar"
SET property: Campaign = "webinar-perf-mar2026"
PRIORITY = medium
```

Owen Lee: Any paid-ads constraints? Need to know if we must include disclaimers or character limits for Google.

Nina Park: Keep headlines < 30 chars for paid, descriptions < 90. No regulatory disclaimers needed for this campaign.

design-bot: Export tokens: PNG web: sRGB, @1x @2x; SVG for charts (optimized); PDF print: CMYK 300dpi; PPTX export from Figma. File naming convention: <asset>-<size>-<tag> e.g. hero-desktop-webinar-perf-2026@2x.png

Kai Torres: I'll sketch comps today. ETA: first draft Figma link by Fri EOD. If we need to move quicker, I can do a lightweight hero variant + one infographic by Thu.

Priya Malhotra: I'll drop translation spreadsheet and alt-text CSV by Fri noon. Also prepping suggested email subject lines and a small social experiment plan (A/B two CTAs).

Nina Park: Please tag all exported files with marketing tags: webinar-perf-mar2026, benchmark-1pager-2026. Also add a small metadata JSON for analytics with fields: asset_id, created_by, export_date, tags (we'll script ingestion).

Owen Lee: Note for the visual appendix: include raw CSV as downloadable link and a short methodology blurb (2-3 sentences) for transparency.

Kai Torres: Sounds good. Any objections to using a dark hero variant + light variant for accessibility testing?

Nina Park: No objections — include both. Make sure AA contrast for body. Great work team, thanks.

Priya Malhotra: 👍 I'll compile everything into the campaign brief once assets are in place.

Owen Lee: ping me when Figma is ready and I'll grab SVGs for the blog.

design-bot: Auto-note: page "exports" created with frames labeled for each deliverable.

Nina Park: Thanks all — stretching for a quick turnaround but this will pair well with the webinar schedule.
